Issued at 224 AM CDT Tue Oct 13 2026

Through Tonight... Surface high pressure and broad upper ridging 
will maintain lower-mid 90s heat and low afternoon RHs of less than 
30% across the east. A "Limited" fire danger threat continues 
throughout the area. Early this morning, radiational cooling and 
returning low level moisture create conditions conducive for dense 
patchy fog across the southern MS/LA across the HWY-84 corridor. To 
the west across central and northern Louisiana, returning moisture 
will support chances for showers and thunderstorms mainly west of 
our forecast area. Cannot rule out a few moving into parts of 
northeast Louisiana, but will still be combating the deeper 
atmospheric mixing. Overnight lows tonight will drop into the upper 
50s to low 60s. /KP/

Wednesday and Thursday...

Weather conditions will be generally quiet and dry across our entire 
forecast area on Wednesday. Near term guidance continues to show a 
mean ridge around 592-594DM that will flatten and build to the 
northeast. Winds will be light and southerly across our CWA with 
wind gusts under 10 kts. In addition to the light southerly winds, 
sky cover will be generally clear across our CWA on Wednesday. The 
combination of clear skies and sufficient daytime heating will allow 
for afternoon highs to peak into the low to mid 90s across the area. 
Several spots could see some new record temperatures being set 
especially if warmer guidance over performs. Wednesday night will 
remain quiet with overnight lows dipping into the low to mid 60s 
under clear skies. Similar conditions are expected again on Thursday 
with highs in the low to mid 90s.   

Regarding the fire danger for the rest of this work week, there is 
enough afternoon mixing and drop in afternoon humidity into critical 
levels. Deep mixing will allow for minimum afternoon relative 
humidity levels to dip (25 to 35 percent range) most afternoons 
throughout the week, so "Limited" fire danger should persist 
Wednesday through Thursday, especially given light rain totals from 
Isaias. High pressure will keep winds relatively light and should 
limit greater fire concerns throughout the work week.

Friday through Monday...

A stout dry cold front will push into the region by Friday and will 
cause dewpoints to fall into the mid 30s to mid 40s. At the very 
least, cool down still remains likely next weekend. Highs will be 
seasonably warm Friday in the upper 80s to low 90s, with lows in the 
low to mid 60s that morning and lows that night upper 40s to low 50s 
north of Interstate 20 (48-52F) to mid to upper 50s (53-57F) to the 
south. Seasonable and pleasant fall temperatures will build areawide 
into next weekend. 

The combination of continued drought stressed vegetation and 
longstanding limited rainfall will help increase fire danger 
concerns. 1035-1045mb surface high building will build east out of 
the lee side of the Rockies through the Midwest, leading to 6-8mb 
pressure gradient and resultant gusty gradient wind/wind gusts 
reaching 30 mph at times. A "Limited" gusty wind threat will likely 
be added for the area. The Storm Prediction Center has highlighted a 
relatively rare (for our area) Marginal Outlook for fire conditions 
on Friday with the expected dry cold frontal passage. We will be 
refining our messaging for fire danger locally, but do expect more 
Elevated wording for Friday's fire danger after several lower 
end/"Limited" days this week. Low chances for scattered showers 
(PoPs around 15%) will be possible across portions of west MS, 
southwest MS, and portions of northeast LA heading into Monday. 
/KP/CR/NF/
